config.grain_rationale: Each record is one registered (or former) company name of an ASIC-registered body, identified by its ACN. A company whose name has changed appears as its current record (Current Name Indicator = Y, Company Name = the current registered name) plus one or more former-name records (Current Name Indicator blank, Company Name = the former name, Current Name = the name it was changed to, Current Name Start Date = when the new name took effect). All records for an ACN therefore describe the same legal entity; the entity attribute mapped from Company Name is a name claim whose validity ends when the name was superseded.

record_id.rationale: ACN alone repeats across name-history rows (471 distinct ACNs in 473 discovery records), so the ACN + the name on the row identifies one record uniquely; name columns are trimmed first.

fields.rationale: ASIC's registered company name (the name on the ASIC register), flagged as the current name by Current Name Indicator=Y. Validity starts at the registration date (left-padded source value trimmed).

Historical registered name: rows without the current-name flag carry a former name, and Current Name Start Date gives the date the successor name took effect, i.e. when this former name stopped being the registered name (observed: LOVINI HOLDINGS PTY LTD -> MONAKA PTY LTD on 28/01/2016).
Current Name on a former-name row states the name the company adopted on Current Name Start Date; emitting it with valid_from = that date records the successor legal name from this history row.
ASIC ACN column, 9 digits in all sampled rows and 100% checksum-valid on the discovery partition.
ASIC ABN column; 11-digit checksum-valid for populated values, and the placeholder '0' (145 rows) means no ABN recorded, so it is nulled before the abn transform. Not derived from ACN.

Type states the ASIC body type explicitly: APTY = Australian proprietary company and APUB = Australian public company (both -> company), which are the only values present in the discovery partition (APTY 458, APUB 15). Codes seen for foreign/registered bodies in the raw preview (FNOS, e.g. 'BANQUE NATIONALE DE PARIS') are not company types under the ontology list and map to other; anything unrecognised defaults to unknown.

ASIC status codes observed: REGD (registered -> active), DRGD (deregistered), EXAD (external administration -> nearest allowed value in_liquidation), SOFF (struck off -> deregistered). Unlisted codes fall back to unknown.

The state in which the body was registered (ASIC 'Previous State of Registration'); a jurisdiction attribute, not a current street address. Normalised through the state enum (NSW/VIC/QLD/WA/SA/TAS + ACT/NT); values outside the AU/NZ set become OTHER.

constants.rationale: Source is the ASIC Australian company register, so the registration jurisdiction is Australia. Low-moderate: the dataset also contains a few foreign-registered bodies (Type FNOS), for which AU is the registering country rather than the entity's home country.

unmapped.reason: ASIC class code (LMSH limited by shares, LMGT limited by guarantee) has no ontology target; it is not needed to determine entity_type (Type is sufficient) so it is left unmapped rather than folded into a combined field.
ASIC sub-class code (PROP proprietary, PSTC public non-listed, ULSN/ULST/LISN/LIST etc.) has no ontology target; it is not an ANZSIC industry code and not a clean sole_trader/trust signal.
State-level registration number for the body; not an ABN/ACN/NZBN and has no ontology target (its digits partially pass the ACN checksum by chance only).

Would date the end of registration, but the ontology has no slot for registration end; deregistration status already flows to entity.status, and using it as record valid_to would wrongly terminate the legal_name/ACN claims. Left out to avoid over-claiming.
Empty in every discovery record; no information.
Row-level flag used as a condition to distinguish current from former names; not an entity attribute itself.
Used only as the validity date for the name claims (valid_from of Current Name / valid_to of Company Name); not an entity attribute.
Mapped (see fields) only under the former-name condition; it is a name claim of the same legal entity, not a trading name.

config.notes: Tab-delimited CSV inside the ZIP (COMPANY_202611.csv), utf-8-sig. Name columns are space-padded in the raw data, hence trim/collapse_whitespace. One legal entity usually appears as 1-2 rows (current name + former name(s)); dedupe downstream on ACN. Type codes beyond APTY/APUB/FNOS were not observed in the discovery partition and are best guesses; unrecognised types default to unknown.

fields.reason: ASIC Company Name is the registered legal name; emitting the (trimmed) name with validity ending at Current Name Start Date for former-name rows is a correct name claim.

Current Name on a former-name row is the successor registered legal name; emitting it with valid_from = Current Name Start Date is correct. Note a data oddity (KNIGHT FRANK (NSW) PTY LTD dated 15/09/2026) but the mapping logic is right.
11-digit ABN with '0' placeholder nulled first; checksums validate and the last 9 digits happen to match ACN for these bodies as expected.

APTY/APUB -> company and RACN -> incorporated_association are defensible explicit code mappings. But mapping multiple foreign/other codes (FNOS, ARBN, ITDN, NOAC, ACNC, QLCS, ADFA) all to 'other' by guess is risky; some (e.g. ACNC/QLCS are registered bodies, ARBN is a foreign company registration) may really be company/incorporated_association or unknown. Default-to-unknown is fine; the non-company codes should not be silently collapsed to 'other' without evidence.

REGD->active, DRGD->deregistered, SOFF->deregistered are correct; EXAD->in_liquidation is a reasonable nearest-value mapping (external administration is broader than liquidation, but acceptable approximation; could be flagged).
dd/mm/yyyy parsed day-first; all sampled values (30/04/1907, 22/03/1968, 23/01/1882) yield plausible dates with no day/month ambiguity issues.

This is the state of registration jurisdiction, not a current business/premises address state. Mapping it to address.state conflates registration jurisdiction with address; the rationale acknowledges it is not a street address but the target semantics (address.state) are still a stretch. Values (NSW, SA, VIC, QLD) normalise correctly though, and one row with empty value correctly emits nothing.

Constant AU is reasonable for an ASIC register but wrong for foreign-registered bodies (e.g. BANQUE NATIONALE DE PARIS, Type FNOS) where AU is the registration country not the entity's country. The mapping itself concedes this.

missed.reason: Population of this column is a direct, explicit signal of deregistration and should override/strengthen status; the rationale's concern about valid_to is valid but the value should still feed status rather than being wholly discarded.

LMGT (limited by guarantee) vs LMSH (limited by shares) is a useful corroborating signal; NLIA on SEAMET LTD indicates no-liability company, which may warrant 'other'/company disambiguation rather than ignoring. At minimum it is evidence for entity_type.
Already mapped, but EXAD could be surfaced with the raw code recorded rather than only approximated as in_liquidation.

critic.summary: Core identifier mappings (legal_name from Company Name and Current Name history, ACN, ABN with placeholder handling, date_registered day-first, status codes) are sound. Main concerns: entity_type collapses several heterogeneous non-company ASIC codes to 'other' by guess (doubtful, especially ARBN/ACNC/QLCS), address.state is really registration jurisdiction rather than a postal/premises address state (doubtful), and the constant address.country=AU is wrong for foreign bodies. Date of Deregistration was discarded though it is a strong explicit deregistration signal that should feed status.
